item.title: Apple Has a Software Problem + Nvidia’s CEO Crisis with Joanna Stern
item.description:
In this episode of Power On, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman is joined by technology journalist and reviewer Joanna Stern of The New Things and NBC News for a critical look at Apple’s software leadership and its struggles to compete in artificial intelligence. They discuss whether software chief Craig Federighi’s management style and Apple’s rigid development processes are holding the company back, why Siri continues to fail at basic tasks and whether Apple needs to start over with a new AI assistant. They also examine how Apple’s AI shortcomings have delayed major hardware products. Plus, their experiences with the iPhone Duo, its new face-unlock feature, Joanna’s HomeView review and whether Apple’s Johny Srouji could be a candidate to lead Nvidia following its leadership crisis.
Have a question for Mark? Email us at poweron@bloomberg.net or join the Power On Discord Subscribe to the Power On Newsletter at https://www.bloomberg.com/poweron (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic Investor Sees Opportunity Beyond IPO
item.description: Anthropic shares opened at $111.50, roughly 34% above their $83 IPO price, after the company completed the biggest IPO in history. Baillie Gifford’s Peter Singlehurst says the debut is just one milestone in a much longer investment story, with Anthropic’s opportunity driven both by increasingly capable models and the spread of existing AI technology deeper into enterprises. He also discusses why the firm plans to remain a long-term shareholder as Anthropic moves from the private to public markets. He joins Ed Ludlow from the Nasdaq on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Apple’s iPhone Camera and Photos Software Chief Jon McCormack Leaves Company
item.description: Apple Inc.’s head of camera and photo software has left, marking a rare shake-up in the leadership behind one of the iPhone’s most important features.
item.dc:creator: Mark Gurman

item.title: Electronics Industry Faces Global Circuit Board Shortage
item.description: The worldwide economy is staring down a gaping shortage of a foundational component found in nearly every consumer product that contains electronics, according to a new advisory from the Global Electronics Association.
item.dc:creator: Kelcee Griffis

item.title: Anthropic IPO Provides Cash to Continue R&D Spending, CFO Says
item.description: Anthropic PBC’s public market debut will allow the company to keep investing to stay ahead on AI, as the Claude chatbot maker devotes about 75% of its computing capacity to research and development, Anthropic Chief Financial Officer Krishna Rao said Thursday.
item.dc:creator: Rebecca Torrence

item.title: Google Workers Urge Bosses to Give Schools Search Without AI
item.description: Hundreds of Google employees are urging the tech giant to curb its aggressive approach to rolling out artificial intelligence in K-12 schools.
item.dc:creator: Julia Love

item.title: Zino: Anthropic is Most Important IPO That I've Seen
item.description:
Anthropic shares are set to soar when they start trading on Thursday, after the artificial intelligence lab’s $107.3 billion IPO and private placement broke SpaceX’s record for the biggest-ever offering.
Anthropic’s debut shifts the spotlight in the AI investment boom from companies making the tools to run the most advanced models to the model makers themselves. With hundreds of billions of dollars committed to infrastructure such as chips and data centers, the next test for the top AI labs is to grow revenue fast enough to outpace the industry’s ambitious spending plans.
Angelo Zino, Senior Equity Analyst, Senior Vice President at CFRA, discusses Anthropic's return on investment. He speaks with Bloomberg's Paul Sweeney and Scarlet Fu. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nasdaq Expects Smooth Anthropic IPO, Griggs Says
item.description: Nelson Griggs, president of Nasdaq, discusses how the Nasdaq has captured three of the biggest IPOs in history - SpaceX, SK Hynix and now Anthropic. He talks about the ANT listing and what to expect once shares start trading. He joins Ed Ludlow from the Nasdaq on "Bloomberg Tech." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Ledger CTO Guillemet to Depart for New Security Venture
item.description: Ledger SAS’s longtime Chief Technology Officer Charles Guillemet announced his departure from the crypto hardware maker, weeks after the company suffered a high-profile hardware attack.
item.dc:creator: Emma Haidar

item.title: Anthropic CFO on 'Democratizing Access' to Company Stock
item.description: As Anthropic arrives on Wall Street in a deal set to raise a record $107.3 billion, Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao explains what this record-breaking listing means for the company. He discusses Anthropic's "disciplined" investment strategy on compute, the company's resilience to market conditions, and conservative approach to its balance sheet. He joins Bloomberg Tech's Ed Ludlow from the Nasdaq on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: How Anthropic Plans to Use IPO Proceeds
item.description: Anthropic CFO Krishna Rao says the company will continue to invest in computing with the proceeds from their IPO during an interview with Ed Ludlow on "Bloomberg Open Interest." (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic IPO Delivers Wall Street Windfall
item.description: Anthropic’s blockbuster IPO is set to pay Wall Street banks $550 million, topping the fees from SpaceX. But the bigger prize may come after the offering: Goldman Sachs and Morgan Stanley could win wealthy employees as clients, while strong investor demand offers a snapshot of capital markets and AI momentum. Bloomberg’s Chief Wall Street Correspondent Sridhar Natarajan joins Bloomberg Open Interest for the latest. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Nvidia is 'Biggest Case of Industrial Espionage' in US Stock Market History, Says George Noble
item.description: Nvidia Corp. sought to deliver a clear message during its first earnings update since the departure of longtime leader Jensen Huang: He’s not coming back, and the company will be fine without him. The chip giant boosted its sales forecast for next year and vowed to improve Nvidia’s access to critical supplies, while tamping down speculation that Huang might return. The company also added $150 billion to its stock-buyback program. George Noble, Managing Partner at Noble Capital Advisors and former Fidelity Fund Manager, offers his bearish AI take on Anthropic and Nvidia. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Why Anthropic May Be Takeover-Proof
item.description: Jones Day Global Chair of M&A Robert Profusek joins Bloomberg Open Interest to explain how Anthropic’s public-benefit mission, founder voting control,and safety commitments could shape investor protections and make the AI company difficult to take over. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Anthropic’s Safety Pledges Questioned by Tech Leaders, Scientists
item.description: A coalition of tech leaders and scientists have signed “The Misanthropic Statement,” an open letter questioning Anthropic’s commitment to AI safety. Rumman Chowdhury, CEO and founder at Humane Intelligence PBC, discusses the group’s concerns on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Corrects spelling of guest’s name in description.) (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: AI Financing Shifts From Hyperscalers to Chips: Berro
item.description: Kelsey Berro, fixed income portfolio manager at JPMorgan Asset Management, says record demand has absorbed a surge in hyperscaler debt, but the next test for AI financing will come from chips. “2027, it’s gonna be about the chip financing,” Berro says on “Bloomberg Surveillance.” (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Was Warned of Telecoms Risk Years Before Salt Typhoon Hack
item.description: CISA fought to block release of report laying out ‘perilous’ situation with US telecommunication networks.
item.dc:creator: Ryan Gallagher

item.title: Bitcoin Pares Gain as Anthropic Fails to Sustain Risk Appetite
item.description: Bitcoin pared gains after Anthropic PBC’s market debut failed to sustain enthusiasm for the artificial-intelligence trade, weighing on most riskier assets.
item.dc:creator: Emily Nicolle and Micah Barkley

item.title: Alibaba Sees Cloud Rebound After In-House Chips Offset US Curbs
item.description: Alibaba Group Holding Ltd.’s chief executive officer said the company’s increasing reliance on in-house technology should offset the impact of US restrictions on cutting-edge American chips, as he worked to dispel concerns about Washington’s latest curbs.
item.dc:creator: Luz Ding

item.title: European Stocks Decline in Longest Losing Streak Since August
item.description: European stocks fell for a fourth straight day, weighed down by defensive sectors, as investors awaited the start of trading in Anthropic PBC’s shares after a blockbuster initial public offering.
item.dc:creator: Rivaldo Jantjies and Rose Henderson
